free_tier.stated: no service and no account; it is a configuration recipe plus a shell script

egress.terms: not applicable; the recipe states no volume; ingress: tcp

chaining: identical to wstunnel: needs a server host, then rides a websocket-capable forwarder.
binding_note: the constraint is the same host as wstunnel, since this project adds no code of its own; the recipe says 'droplet'

identity_cost.detail: no account; the server is a droplet the recipe assumes the reader already has

reliability_note: the client script edits /etc/hosts and reloads dnsmasq; a stale entry survives a failed tunnel start
confidence_note: nothing to raise: it is a recipe whose only executable part is wstunnel, which is recorded on its own rung

evidence.proved: "No modifications need to be made to the Wireguard server configuration itself, but wstunnel needs to be installed", and the systemd unit with --restrict-to 127.0.0.1:51820

notes: Counted separately because brief names it, but it is not a second implementation: it installs wstunnel, writes a unit file, and wraps wg-quick with a script that rewrites the peer endpoint. Its only unique contribution is the wstunnel.sh wrapper that rewrites /etc/hosts and the interface config, which the wstunnel README does by hand.

extras.wg_detail: "Wireguard VPN connection to be tunnelled over a secure websockets connection"; the recipe runs wstunnel, not new software: 'wstunnel server wss://0.0.0.0:443 --restrict-to 127.0.0.1:51820'
extras.volume_stated: not applicable; the recipe states no volume
extras.transit_note: the same bytes as wstunnel, through a host the reader is assumed to rent
extras.hosting_requirement: a server host with wstunnel and the WireGuard listener, described in the recipe as a droplet
